articles.headline: Union Anti-Slavery Society -- third quarterly meeting (Report of the Board of Managers)
articles.summary: Report of the third quarterly meeting of the Union Anti-Slavery Society of Philadelphia, adjourned from Feb. 28 and held at Clarkson Hall on a Thursday evening (14th inst.). The President, Rev. J. M. Willson, took the chair; Corresponding Secretary Samuel D. Hastings read the Report of the Board of Managers, which laments that the professing church has become the 'strong hold' of slavery and pledges to go forward regardless of favor or frown. After debate the report was adopted and ordered sent to every minister of the Gospel in the community, and an amendment to the 4th article of the constitution was laid over.

articles.headline: Colored citizens renew their protest against colonization
articles.summary: Reprinting the caustic Colonization Convention notice from the Christian Witness of Pittsburgh, the Freeman observes that 'the colored people of Boston, New York, Philadelphia, and Pittsburgh have within a few weeks renewedly protested in the most solemn manner against the colonization scheme, and declared their unalterable determination to be neither wheedled nor driven from the land of their nativity.'

articles.headline: Philadelphia City Anti-Slavery Society -- annual election of officers by ward
articles.summary: Proceedings of the Philadelphia City Anti-Slavery Society's annual meeting, at which officers were chosen for the ensuing year and Superintendents assigned by ward -- a snapshot of the society's ward organization across the old city (Upper and Lower Delaware, High Street, and Chesnut Wards).
